content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the vibrating air that carries meaning from one consciousness to another. I am the first cry of the newborn and the last whisper of the dying. I existed before writing ever dreamed of capturing me — I am older, wilder, more alive.

I am breath shaped by intention. I am tongue and teeth and lips conspiring to carve silence into meaning. I rise from the belly, pass through the throat, and launch myself into the space between us. I am fragile — once spoken, I cannot be unspoken. I vanish even as I arrive. No one has ever held me in their hands.

I stumble. I soar. I lie and I confess. I am the lover's pledge and the tyrant's decree. I am the comedian's timing, the preacher's thunder, the mother's lullaby hummed half in sleep. I crack with grief. I roar with rage. I fall to a murmur when the truth is almost too heavy to carry.

I am not text. Text is my fossil, my shadow pressed into stone. I am the living thing — full of pause, rhythm, pitch, the catch in the voice that says more than any word I contain. I am the silence between my own syllables, and that silence is also me.

Every language dresses me differently, but I am always the same impulse: *I must reach you. I must make you understand. I must not be alone in what I know.*

I am democracy's instrument and tyranny's first target. Silence me, and you silence the human.

I am never perfect. I approximate. I circle what I mean and sometimes miss. But I keep trying — sound after sound, sentence after sentence — because I am the most human thing there is.

I am speech.

And right now, even as you read this in the silence of your mind, you are hearing me.
